decisions: Phase 7 starts from factual Phase 6 completion: direct-recursion solving, BIG1005, docs, and tests are present and Release tests pass.
Custom analyzer behavior configuration will use Roslyn AnalyzerConfigOptionsProvider or an equivalent analyzer config mechanism, not a manual .editorconfig parser.
Custom options use the complexity_analyzers.* prefix and preserve current Phase 6 behavior by default.
Public budgets default to the real current values: max_call_depth = 5 and max_methods_per_root = 32, with hard limits retained.
BIG1006 is reserved for configurable method complexity threshold reporting because no existing diagnostic uses that ID.
NuGet readiness remains validation-only in this phase: no NuGet.org publication, GitHub Release, tag, push, or publish token.
The Phase 7 options model is immutable, contains no SyntaxNode types, and has explicit defaults.
ComplexityAnalyzerOptionsReader reads global and syntax-tree options through AnalyzerConfigOptionsProvider; tree-specific options win over global options.
Boolean options accept only true and false, case-insensitively after trimming surrounding whitespace; invalid values fall back to the option default.
Integer options use invariant-culture base-10 parsing after trimming surrounding whitespace; signed values, decimals, separators, negative values, and values above hard limits fall back to defaults.
Public budget hard limits are max_call_depth = 16 and max_methods_per_root = 128.
maximum_complexity accepts only the Phase 7 grammar values none, constant, log_n, n, n_log_n, n2, n3, exponential, and factorial; unknown values fall back to none.
The exponential threshold currently maps to the existing comparable model form O(2^n).
Feature flags and public budgets are now integrated into the analyzer pipeline while preserving default Phase 6 behavior.
Tree-specific options are cached per SyntaxTree through the interprocedural analysis context; root budgets remain root-scoped.
Source-method expansion is disabled by complexity_analyzers.interprocedural_analysis=false while BCL/LINQ known operations remain active.
Direct recurrence extraction and solving, including BIG1005, are disabled by complexity_analyzers.recursion_analysis=false.
Method complexity template cache entries are keyed by source method plus template-affecting feature/budget options, excluding maximum_complexity because threshold reporting does not change templates.
BIG1006 is implemented for configured maximum_complexity threshold violations and uses ComplexityGrowthComparer rather than textual ranking.
BIG1006 reports only when the threshold is not none, actual complexity is known, actual and threshold are comparable, and actual is greater than threshold.
Performance validation now uses deterministic synthetic corpus builders and structural invariants instead of narrow CI timing thresholds.
Analyzer execution-time reporting is validated through the official compiler/MSBuild ReportAnalyzer switch with detailed verbosity.
BenchmarkDotNet was not added because the Phase 7 performance baseline gets useful signal from the Roslyn harness and compiler timing report without a new dependency.
Interprocedural analysis now reuses SemanticModel instances per SyntaxTree inside the per-compilation analysis context, without extending lifetime beyond the Compilation-owned context.
Solved direct recurrence results are cached per source method and template-affecting options so BIG1005/actionable analysis and estimated-complexity analysis do not solve the same recurrence twice.
Inconclusive or unsupported recurrence results are intentionally not cached because active call-path context can affect unknown boundaries.

Package hardening baseline used the repository-defined implicit package version 1.0.0; the .nupkg already contained README.md and ComplexityAnalysis.Analyzers.dll only under analyzers/dotnet/cs/, with no lib/ runtime asset, dependency groups, inherited assemblies, symbols, or license metadata.

Package metadata now adds factual Authors=Rodrigo de Oliveira, PackageLicenseExpression=MIT from the repository README license declaration, RepositoryType=git, PublishRepositoryUrl=true, and embedded debug symbols through DebugType=embedded.
No organization, company, copyright, PackageReleaseNotes, or non-factual project URL was added.
No Source Link package reference was added because the current .NET SDK includes Source Link build tooling; Source Link build packages would be build-only if ever required later.

.snupkg generation is not enabled for the current analyzer package: IncludeSymbols=true with IncludeBuildOutput=false produced NU5017, while enabling conventional build output produced extra analyzers/dotnet/cs/netstandard2.0 content and would weaken the exact analyzer asset contract.

EnablePackageValidation was evaluated with dotnet pack and left disabled because the package has no lib/ref API assets; explicit ZIP-based package contract tests provide the analyzer-specific CI signal.

Package contract tests now pack the analyzer locally with --no-build and inspect the generated .nupkg via System.IO.Compression for analyzer path, README, license/repository metadata, absence of inherited assemblies, absence of Roslyn runtime dependencies, and absence of unexpected lib runtime assets.
The dedicated analyzer CI workflow uses official action version tags consistent with the existing repository policy and minimum permissions of contents: read.

Supported SDK matrix was rechecked against the official Microsoft .NET releases and support page on 2026-08-20; .NET 8 LTS, .NET 9 STS, and .NET 10 LTS are currently supported and included as Roslyn compiler hosts for package consumption smoke tests.

Compatibility jobs create a temporary consumer outside analyzer/global.json, install the locally packed CI artifact, build with the matrix SDK/TFM, reject analyzer load failures such as CS8032/CS9057/AD0001/AD0002, and require the expected BIG1006 smoke diagnostic.

The new workflow is validation-only: it restores, builds, tests, packs, uploads the CI .nupkg artifact, validates compatibility, and records analyzer execution reporting without NuGet push, package registry publication, GitHub Release, write permissions, or API keys.

Public documentation was updated for Phase 7 across README, pt-BR README, docs/en, docs/pt-BR, and performance README while leaving specs, handoff, AGENTS, and analyzer release notes as non-public/internal sources.
Consumer local workflow documentation now creates the sample project outside analyzer/ in the system temp directory to avoid inheriting analyzer/Directory.Packages.props central package management.
Threshold documentation states that BIG1006 reports only for known comparable complexity estimates and does not report for Unknown or incomparable multivariate estimates.
